newsitem.title: USA: PECO seeks random participant selection.
newsitem.headline: PECO seeks random participant selection.

text.p: PECO Energy Co said the retail wheeling pilot proposal it filed with the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission calls for a neutral third party will randomly select customers from across all rate classes.

The third party will also select a political subdivision in Philadelphia and one township or borough in the suburbs from a pool of eligible localities. All residential customers in the two selected localities will be eligible for the pilot.
The third party will also select commercial and industrial customers, using a total of 75 megawatts of electricity, from Enterprise Zones in the City and suburbs.
The selection will take place between April 1 and May 1, or after the commission approves PECO Energy's filing.
Once selected, an eligible customer can make a decision to choose a new supplier at any time until September 1998.

PECO said it will send information about the pilot and how to participate to all customers selected, as well as a form authorizing the release of the customer's name, address and telephone number to electric suppliers. If the release is not authorized, pilot customers will be sent a list of participating suppliers so the customers can contact the suppliers if they choose.
All electric suppliers participating in pilot programs in Pennsylvania will have to be approved by the Commonwealth and licensed by the commission.

If pilot customers decide they do not want to select another supplier, PECO will continue to supply their electricity. The selected customers will retain the option of choosing another supplier at a later date during the pilot.

Customers selecting a new supplier will also enter into a contract with that supplier for a minimum of 30 days. During the pilot, eligible customers can switch to another outside supplier, or return to PECO. If they return, they cannot choose another supplier during the pilot period.
A customer could only switch suppliers at the end of a contract or if the supplier failed to live up to the contract.
In a case where a supplier fails to deliver the agreed-upon power, PECO said, it would step in to assure uninterrupted electric supply.

Pilot customers could be billed separately by the outside supplier for energy consumed, or the energy supplier could request PECO to do the billing. In either case, PECO will bill the customer for its delivery services.
